/**
 * AF3's reference conformers for the eight nucleotide components, baked.
 *
 * Generated by tools/oracle/dump_reference_conformers.py --nucleic - do not
 * hand-edit. The protein table beside this one is reference-conformers.js, and
 * everything its header says applies here: these come from AF3's own featuriser
 * rather than from a chemistry library, so the atom order, the dense-slot
 * indices, the four-character names, the elements and the charges are AF3's by
 * construction - and the conformer is ONE SAMPLE of torsions AF3 resamples per
 * residue instance.
 *
 * 🔴 A NUCLEOTIDE IS THE MIRROR IMAGE OF AN AMINO ACID, AT THE OTHER END. A
 * protein residue gains an OXT at its C-terminus and its N-terminal form is the
 * internal one; a nucleotide gains OP3 at its 5-prime end - the phosphate
 * oxygen an internal residue trades for the bond to the one before it - and its
 * 3-prime form IS the internal one. Measured for all eight, not assumed.
 *
 * 🔴 AND THE ONE-LETTER CODES COLLIDE WITH THE AMINO ACIDS. A, C and G are
 * alanine, cysteine and glycine in a protein chain and adenine, cytosine and
 * guanine in a nucleic one, so nothing here may be looked up without knowing
 * which kind of chain the residue came from. That is why these are separate
 * tables rather than more entries in the protein one.
 *
 * Each atom is [slot, name, element, charge, x, y, z]; `rigid` is
 * [i, j, distance] over indices into `internal`.
 */
